title: The saloks to Mardana
hookLine: a few saloks are headed with Mardana's name, generally read as Nanak's words to him (Bihagra ki Var, ang 553)

cards: Mardana. In the Sikh stories he is close by: Guru Nanak's companion on the road, a Muslim musician with a rebab, playing while Nanak sang. Yesterday's minstrels came later.
Now open the Guru Granth Sahib to Bihagra ki Var, Ang 553. Among the saloks there, a few carry Mardana's name in the heading. They're generally read as Nanak's words to him, friend to friend.

teach.h: THE AGE IS THE JAR, DESIRE THE WINE.
teach.b: The saloks begin with a picture a friend might use to tease you awake. In paraphrase: this dark age is the wine jar, desire is the wine, and the mind is the one drinking it.
Anger is the cup, filled with attachment, and ego is the one pouring. Drink in that company, and you're ruined. Strong words.
But Nanak doesn't just take the cup away. He offers a different brew.

teach.h: A DIFFERENT BREW: DEEDS, TRUTH, GOODNESS.
teach.b: In paraphrase again: make good deeds the vat, truth the sweetener, and truth itself the finest wine. Make goodness the bread and good conduct the butter. That's the drink, he says, that wipes away wrongdoing.

teach.h: NOT SCOLDING THE THIRST: REDIRECTING IT.
teach.b: So the saloks don't scold the thirst. They redirect it: whatever pulls at you, desire, the need to be filled, take that same longing and point it at truth. Now the heading.

Readers differ on what the name Mardana is doing there: whether the words are spoken to him, or carry his name for another reason. The tradition generally hears them as words to a friend, and that changes how they sound.
These aren't lines shouted at a crowd.
They're what you say to someone you've walked with for years, who can take hard words because they know you love them.
Friends name the cup in your hand. Then they hand you a better one.

how: Sikhs remember Bhai Mardana as Guru Nanak's companion and rebab player, and the saloks headed with his name in Bihagra ki Var are read and sung as part of that Var.

games.q: your friend is pouring a drink that's ruining them. what do the saloks do?
o: knock the cup away and leave.
name the cup, then offer a better one.
games.why: the saloks name desire as the wine and ego as the one pouring, then offer a new brew: good deeds, truth, goodness.

practice: Bring to mind a friend who has walked with you a long way, and a moment they told you something true you didn't want to hear, or a moment you wish you had. Notice how kindness and honesty can sit in the same sentence.
If you pray, rest there with Waheguru on the breath out.

wordCard.voice: Mardana. Guru Nanak's companion and rebab player, generally heard as the friend addressed in these saloks: trade the old cup for the wine of truth.

carryVoice: Your line: words to a friend. Hard words land softest from someone who loves you. Day seven hundred ninety-three.
